This post is intended more for beginners.

So why only one dumbbell? Two main reasons.

* It's cheap. Buying one dumbbell won't break your bank. * It's portable. You can easily take one dumbbell with you, meaning you can do your workout anywhere.

What are the dumbbell exercises?

1. Concentration Curls https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dgvKbfP6lTU 1. Seated One Arm Tricep Extensions https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrD3CHAWxQY 1. One Arm Dumbbell Flys https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aAYM4GAFqGs 1. One Arm Dumbbell Rows https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KR8onsa5jFQ 1. Goblet Squats https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MeIiIdhvXT4

There are plenty more exercises you can do with a dumbbell, but I feel that those 5 cover the basics well enough.

"I don't want to carry a dumbbell everywhere I go. What are some basic and effective muscle building exercises you can do without it?"

Here are a few basic exercises everyone should be familiar with:

1. Pushups 1. Chair Dips 1. Normal Squats 1. Sit Ups 1. Leg Raises 1. Planks 1. Pull Ups and Chin Ups (assuming you have access to a sturdy bar, I highly recommend these)

Don't feel bad if you have to look any of these up. Proper form is important, and looking things up can really pay off, especially since there are many variations on each exercise to discover. Pushups alone have seemingly endless variations, so you should do yourself a favor and search for them.

"I'm out of shape. I can't do all that stuff! I'll kill myself!"

Start small. Do what you can, then stop. Expect soreness. Let yourself heal for a few days. Then try again. Your body will adjust and you will be able to do a little more each time.

Create your own workout routine. Build onto it over time.

Always remember: No excuses. Your body, your responsibility. No whining, just action. Get it done.
